claims.text: The initial TiVNbTa alloy is an as-cast, dendritic, single-phase BCC refractory high-entropy alloy.
The initial TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of about 800 MPa at lower temperature.
The TiVNbTa alloy's yield strength decreases to about 330 MPa at 1273 K.
The baseline alloy reaches about 423 MPa compressive strength at 30% strain and 1273 K.
A minor yttrium addition during processing will promote in-situ formation of Y2O3 precipitates.
The resulting Y2O3 precipitates will be fine, stable, and dispersed throughout the BCC matrix.
Dispersed oxide particles can provide precipitation or dispersion strengthening in a refractory HEA matrix.
The Y2O3 nanoparticles will impede dislocation glide at elevated temperature.
The Y2O3 nanoparticles will impede grain-boundary sliding at elevated temperature.
Precipitation strengthening can improve the elevated-temperature strength of high-entropy alloys.
The yttrium-modified TiVNbTa alloy will retain a yield strength significantly above 330 MPa at 1273 K.
The yttrium-modified alloy will have greater compressive strength at 30% strain and 1273 K than the undoped alloy.
The Y2O3 dispersion will not significantly compromise the alloy's thermal conductivity.
Mechanical alloying followed by spark-plasma sintering can produce a refractory HEA containing an oxygen-derived oxide precipitate phase.
Strength improvement will depend on the uniformity, size, and volume fraction of the Y2O3 precipitates.
A failure to obtain more than a 20% statistically significant increase in yield or compressive strength at 1273 K is defined as a falsifying outcome.

contradictions.description: The reported baseline is explicitly as-cast and dendritic, whereas the proposed control is mechanically alloyed and spark-plasma-sintered. Comparing the modified MA/SPS sample with that processed control is controlled, but it does not directly test improvement relative to the stated as-cast 330 MPa/423 MPa baseline because processing alone may substantially change grain size, phases, and strength.
